races.name: Forte Healthcare Handicap

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Rates as the lone confirmed front-runner here; 14 days since a solid second over 6f on Good at this sort of trip, Dylan Browne McMonagle retains the ride for Mark Fahey, and with no rival likely to push him, the ease of the lead is his chief asset even if his OR-81 is competitive.

runners_data.name: Ohailbhic
runners_data.note: Returned from a 124-day break with back-to-back wins over 7-8f at Sligo onStandrd, so the step back to 6f on Good at Naas is a significant query; Ronan Whelan aboard for a trainer with a modest recent record, and similar-going form runs to only 7 wins/places from 15 efforts.

runners_data.name: Bad Boy Rizz
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this lightly raced three-year-old who has form figures of 2-1-2-3 at 5-6f on Good, suggesting he handles the surface well; the step up from 5f to 6f on this evidence is a plus and his prominent style should see him travel in the right part of the race from the outset.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent runs have all been over 7f on Soft or Standard, making both the shorter trip and the Good going live queries; Adrian McGuinness has been busy (2/28 in 14 days) but this horse's best sim-going figures are only 5/15, limiting confidence.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with a win on Good ground over 5f and a prominent style that should translate to 6f; trainer David Marnane is in fair form (2/20), Nathan Crosse takes the ride, and the extra furlong on faster ground looks an upgrade on recent outings over 5f on Heavier surfaces.

runners_data.name: Four Blondes
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose best finish in sim-going has been a second in a 2/8f on Good, showing she can hit the board on this surface; however, a 20th on her most recent 6f Good run is a red flag, and a slow single-leader pace makes it hard for true closers to generate the late momentum they need.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Returns from a 243-day absence — the longest layoff in this field — and all five career runs have been on Standard ground at Dundalk, so both the surface and going are completely uncharted; Colin Keane is a major positive, but this represents a significant step into the unknown off a long break.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Naturally races prominently and has a 6f Good win on his card, but with multiple prominent types ahead of him in the pecking order he is likely to be shuffled back from his ideal position; blinkers applied, trainer H Rogers in active form (2/5), but style-fit is compromised by the crowded pace picture.

runners_data.name: Mint Man
runners_data.note: Another horse whose natural instinct is to race up with the pace, but the congested prominent positions mean Chris Hayes will likely find him settled in midfield instead; tongue-tie fitted, and recent form figures of 0-8-8-4-7 over 5-6f give little cause for optimism even if he found his spot.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Flags the ⚠ fades in finish marker and, despite wanting to race prominently, is mapped to midfield because this field is overloaded with pace-pressing types; Ben Coen takes the mount for A. Oliver who is in decent form (2/22), but all five recent runs on Good ground have ended in finishes of 4th or worse.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who also carries the ⚠ fades in finish warning — a damaging combination in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo; Gavin Ryan partners the three-year-old on his second run back in 14 days for Mark Fahey, but finishing effort has been his consistent weakness and this race shape is unlikely to generate the strong pace he would need.

races.paceDynamic: I Bid You Ajou is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no serious rival disputing the lead, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the outset rather than be dragged into a war. Bad Boy Rizz, Ohailbhic, and Soulful Diva will press forward to fill prominent positions immediately behind, creating a compact early order rather than a searing pace. This field contains more genuinely prominent-natured horses than can physically occupy those positions — Gotta Catch'em All, Mint Man, and All Hail are true front-rank types but are most likely to be shuffled back to midfield, with Bad Boy Rizz and Soulful Diva the ones best placed to secure the berths directly behind the leader. A controlled, single-pace 6f on Good ground at Naas with a moderate tempo set by one unchallenged front-runner strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream and produce a sustained finish — pace-pressing profiles win here, not deep closers relying on a fast-run race to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If I Bid You Ajou sets an uncontested pace and the field settles in behind without disruption.
scenarios.body: I Bid You Ajou dictates on a clean lead at a moderate clip, preserving enough energy to maintain momentum through the final furlong; horses slotted directly in behind — particularly Bad Boy Rizz and Soulful Diva — get the perfect stalking trip and are first to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Stride Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Bad Boy Rizz or Soulful Diva travel fluidly in second or third and kick before the leader can respond.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop means the race lacks a true test late, and a horse lobbing just off the pace can produce a clean run to the front approaching the final furlong without needing a change of gear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field bunches, allowing a well-positioned midfield horse to benefit from a late sprint.
scenarios.body: Four Blondes or Flaming Rib, dropped in off a steady gallop, could find clear daylight along the rail or widest of all; however, their hold-up style relies on the pace being sharper than one front-runner typically creates over 6f here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is faster than expected and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving genuine closers to mop up.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses like Ninth Crusade or Unidos producing a strong late run, but Unidos flags in the finish and Ninth Crusade returns from 243 days off; the field also lacks the true pace pressure needed to set this up naturally.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Gotta Catch'em All, Mint Man, or All Hail — all natural front-rank types redistributed to midfield — attempt to push forward at the start; if two or more succeed, the early pace intensifies and dramatically changes the race shape from a controlled lead scenario.

Ohailbhic's layoff of 124 days combined with the step back to 6f on Good after winning over 7-8f on Standard is a compound fitness and suitability query — monitor market moves and how sharply he loads at the stalls.

All Hail carries the fades-in-finish flag on every recent Good-ground start; if he does press forward from his drawn position, he risks setting up the race for closers before weakening late, making him a dangerous pace influence rather than a winning prospect.

Ninth Crusade's 243-day absence and exclusive Standard-ground form means Colin Keane will be managing the horse's fitness through the race as much as riding for position — watch where he sits early as an indicator of whether this is a confidence run or a serious first-time-out-on-turf pitch.

Bad Boy Rizz steps up to 6f for the first time on Good ground having been placed at 2f and 3f shorter trips — if he settles smoothly behind I Bid You Ajou in the first two furlongs rather than pulling, his stamina reserves should see him stay on strongly.

races.name: Arqana Irish EBF Marwell Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.note: Won on Good over five furlongs last time under Colin Keane for G M Lyons — trainer firing at 24% over 14 days — and her prominent style puts her ideally placed to track Shesthedevil, though she needs a clean passage through the congested second rank.

runners_data.name: Back To The Lodge
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this sole hold-up runner whose only start resulted in an 11th over six furlongs on Good; she carries a tendency to fade in the finish and has no wins or places, making her a very speculative runner at this level.

runners_data.name: Belle Of The Ball
runners_data.note: Shane Foley-ridden filly who ran well to finish fourth last time in a 6f Good handicap and has a win at five furlongs on Soft; she is a naturally prominent type but the crowded pace map means she is likely to race further back than ideal, tempering expectations.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes the ride on a horse with a solid form line including five runs on Good, winning over five furlongs at this trip; despite being a natural front-rank traveller, the race shape will likely squeeze him toward midfield — his [STYLE_FIT=0.90] tag reflects the positional cost.

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.note: P Twomey's runner won on his only start over five furlongs on Good, making him an unexposed threat; W J Lee can attempt to park him just behind Shesthedevil where the pace map creates the cleanest route to the line.

runners_data.name: Eastern Queen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced filly — just one run, a fifth of five over 5f Good — and her unknown quantity is reflected in the UNKNOWN style tag; Nathan Crosse is a 14-day-cold booking for a trainer with minimal recent runners, and she is mapped to the rear as the least pace-committed runner.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, she won over 6f Good last time under Chris Hayes for Patrick Magee and steps back to five furlongs here; uncontested, she can dictate a sustainable gallop, and her most recent improvement on Good makes her the key pace reference for the entire field.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on Harry Eustace's filly who won on debut over 5f Good and is a genuine speedball; with multiple prominent types already crowding the second rank, she is likely to end up racing further off the pace than her natural style demands, which is a meaningful positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Silent Beauty
runners_data.note: Donagh O'Connor rides for Kevin Philippart De Foy — trainer with three from 12 over 14 days — and this filly won over 6f Soft last time out; she has a prominent style that puts her in the thick of the traffic battle, and her Good ground profile is unproven at the highest level.

runners_data.name: Tropical Crown
runners_data.note: K R Burke's unbeaten filly — won her only start over 5f Good — is represented by Pierre-Louis Jamin and a trainer firing at a strong 19% over 14 days; she has the profile of a horse who can travel prominently and quicken cleanly, making her a natural danger if she avoids the congestion.

races.paceDynamic: Shesthedevil is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down the Naas five-furlong straight on Good ground. Behind her, Concorde Landed, April Mist, Tropical Crown, and Silent Beauty all want prominent positions, creating a congested second rank that could produce bumping and interference two to three furlongs from home. Belle Of The Ball, Shimmering Sun, and Big Negotiator are all naturally prominent types but cannot all claim that position — one or more will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal, blunting their chance. With a lone front-runner setting a sustainable rather than suicidal pace, and Good ground rewarding horses that travel smoothly in behind before quickening, this race shape most strongly favours classy prominent-to-midfield horses who settle just off the pace and produce a clean, uninterrupted run into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Dictates Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil bowls clear unchallenged and sets a controlled, even tempo that rewards those just tracking her.
scenarios.body: Shesthedevil gets it all her own way at a metronomic gallop, and the horses best placed to pounce are those who have settled smoothly in her slipstream without being caught in the prominent-sector traffic; the sustained, honest pace on Good ground over five furlongs will expose any horse that has to work too hard to hold position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion in the prominent group two to three furlongs out causes interference, hampering multiple runners simultaneously.
scenarios.body: Horses forced wide or checked in the bunching phase lose momentum at the critical point, and those who have been pushed slightly off the pace — but find a clean run — are the beneficiaries; Good ground and a flat track mean late acceleration from a fractionally deeper position can be decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil's gallop proves too strong early, she weakens in the final furlong and hold-up runners finish through.
scenarios.body: Eastern Queen, operating at the rear, would need a genuine collapse of the early pace to arrive in time; Back To The Lodge, despite a tendency to fade, could threaten if the pace truly honest, but both are secondary beneficiaries of an unlikely scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses — Belle Of The Ball, Shimmering Sun, Big Negotiator — manage to force their way into their natural positions after all, creating a genuinely hot pace.
scenarios.body: A hotter-than-expected early tempo would compress the field and bring the hold-up horses into play, but since these three are racing partially out of role this outcome is the least probable; the winner in this shape would be a horse with a clean draw and the tactical nous to switch off before unleashing a final-furlong surge.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a scramble for position between Concorde Landed, April Mist, Tropical Crown, and Silent Beauty in the first furlong — four horses all wanting the same second-rank slots creates a genuine interference risk two to three furlongs out.
Shesthedevil's unchallenged lead is the race's fulcrum — if she controls tempo cleanly, she remains a significant factor at the wire despite her lower OR; monitor her early split closely.

Belle Of The Ball, Shimmering Sun, and Big Negotiator are all being squeezed out of their natural positions — any of the three who finds a gap and reasserts onto the pace rail before the two-furlong marker is immediately upgraded as a live danger.

Back To The Lodge finished 11th on her only start and carries a fade warning — Ben Coen will need the pace to collapse completely for her to reach the placed positions, making her a backmarker to track only if the early fractions are exceptionally fast.

Eastern Queen is an unknown quantity with a single run — Nathan Crosse is on a quiet 14-day record for a low-volume trainer, so any market move on this filly before post time warrants attention given the stable's limited public form.

races.name: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Prominent traveller for Colin Keane and G M Lyons who have a strong 14-day strike rate; form figures of 3 and 4 in similar good-ground conditions last two times out suggest she handles this going well, though her recent best has been over 7f and the drop to 6f here is worth querying.

runners_data.name: Fregada
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who returned a 4th on good ground last time and has struggled for a win recently (0 from last 4 on good); Ronan Whelan will need a faster-run race to deliver her into contention from the rear and the sustainable pace set by Soul Love is a concern.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed five times without winning in recent starts but is consistently thereabouts over 5f on good; the step up to 6f here is an unknown — all recent form is over 5f — and Declan McDonogh will need a strong pace to get her into the race from the back.

runners_data.name: Little Queenie
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up mare whose best recent form is over 5-6f on standard/AW ground; her good-ground figures are modest (1W 3P from 7 on good) and she hasn't won on good turf recently, so Robert Whearty will need the race to develop to suit her from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking filly with two recent wins over 5f on good and soft — the move up to 6f is the key question, but J M Sheridan can place her close to the pace where she is dangerous; Denis Gerard Hogan has 2 winners from 23 runners in the 14-day window, underlining a yard in decent form.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 84 and while she is a true hold-up horse by style, she has been mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; her one recent win came over this trip on good ground, but her last five runs show 5th or worse in 4 of them and she needs to find significant improvement here.

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: Arrives with two wins and a second from her last four starts — in fine form — but her natural racing style is prominent and with so many horses vying for that ground, Ben Coen may find her shuffled back from where she operates best; the form is solid regardless, and she handles good going well.

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and the top-rated runner at OR 101; Pierre-Louis Jamin can set his own fractions and the combination of controlling the race and having class in hand makes her a pivotal figure, though Style_Fit flags a slight positional nuance worth noting.

runners_data.name: Coconut Cove
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3-year-old has a hind-gear note and has won over 6f on standard, though good-ground form is limited (0 wins from 3 on good); Jack Mitchell has ridden her recently and she is likely to race prominently, but her OR of 93 places her mid-tier in this field on ratings.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins heading in and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over in the saddle — a positive booking; however, his natural tendency is to race prominently and the sheer number of horses wanting that position means he could find himself further back than ideal, which dilutes the impact of his current winning momentum.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Recent runs show inconsistency (720717) and a 4-day turnaround from her last run is aggressive at this level; J A Stack has a modest 14-day strike rate of 1/6, and while she is a 5f specialist stepping up, her redistribution to midfield means she won't be able to express her natural forward-going style.

runners_data.name: Oh Cecelia
runners_data.note: K J Condon's 3-year-old has the visor on (hg:v) and won over 5f on soft last time — the switch back to 6f good ground requires more stamina than she showed there; Shane Foley is a positive booking, and she is a genuine hold-up horse who has placed three times in similar conditions, representing a credible late-finisher profile.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Has placed three times over 6f on good ground and Gary Carroll keeps the ride for Joseph G Murphy; a prominent racer who has shown consistent mid-table form rather than winning sparkle, but a clean position close to Soul Love could see him run a solid place race over a trip and going that clearly suits.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Three places from five runs on good ground and a recent win over 5f — the form is progressive for Miss Natalia Lupini's yard; Wayne Lordan rides and will want to position her close to the pace where her best form has been achieved, making her a genuine contender if she handles the move from 5f to 6f.

runners_data.name: Yellowstone Lake
runners_data.note: 45 days off the track is the standout concern — the longest absence in the field — and while P Twomey has 2 from 9 runners in the 14-day window, Yellowstone Lake's form over shorter distances and a longer break makes it harder to assess; a true prominent type who will not get an easy position here.

races.paceDynamic: Soul Love is the confirmed front-runner and, with a field this large containing multiple genuine prominent types competing for early position, she is likely to dictate at a sustainable rather than a scorching tempo on good ground over 6f at Naas. Treasure Rose, Dancing Saxon, Yellowstone Lake, and Focaccia are all natural prominent horses who want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy that ground simultaneously — the most likely outcome is that Soul Love leads with Chantez, Sarahmae, Tahcawin, Coconut Cove, and Xerling tracking closely in a compressed bunch behind, while the redistributed prominent types are forced wider or slightly further back than ideal. The hold-up contingent of Oh Cecelia, Fregada, Likedbymike, and Little Queenie will have last run from well off the pace and will need either a strong tempo or a perfectly timed gap that may not materialise with Soul Love controlling proceedings. With a single, confident front-runner setting a manageable clip and a cluster of prominent-to-midfield types right behind her, this race shape most favours horses who can travel in the first four or five and sustain their effort into the final furlong — the prominent-tracking profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soul Love Leads, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Love sets a controlled pace and horses tracking her in the top four get first run from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: Soul Love dictates a fair gallop and the horses camped just behind — Chantez, Sarahmae, Tahcawin — get the clearest passage and sustain the run home on ground that suits their style; the hold-up brigade are left with too much to do from too far back in a non-end-to-end tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed prominent bunch creates a faster-than-expected early pace and the field strings out, creating room for hold-up horses
scenarios.body: A busier than expected pace collapse in the final furlong opens a late run for Oh Cecelia or Likedbymike, who are proven in good-ground 5-6f and have the turn-of-foot to pick off tiring leaders; this is the scenario where the genuine hold-up horses earn their natural role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Hits Form
scenarios.trigger: If one of the displaced prominent types — Dancing Saxon or Xerling — manages to slot in closer than expected and benefits from a prominent-tracking position
scenarios.body: Dancing Saxon has won two on the bounce and, if Dylan Browne McMonagle can nurse him into a competitive early position despite the field depth, his recent sharp form could see him sustain a challenge; Xerling similarly has placed in five of six starts on good ground and has course-compatible form over 5f that could translate to this 6f trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Soul Love's controlled lead is never seriously challenged and she is not overtaken by any horse before the line
scenarios.body: With nobody willing to fire up to press Soul Love in the first 2f, she could build an unassailable advantage and simply sustain it — her OR of 101 is the highest in the field and her record shows she is effective over this exact course and distance combination in this going.

watchPoints.text: Soul Love (P-L Jamin) has the clearest lead at the top of this race and if she gets a clean break and is never headed before the 2f pole, the trackers will be chasing a horse that can sustain her effort — watch whether any horse goes after her early.

Dancing Saxon (D Browne McMonagle) is in strong form with two wins on the bounce but will likely be denied his natural prominent berth in this field — watch his position after the first furlong to assess whether he can recover and still be a factor.

Oh Cecelia (Shane Foley) wears the visor and is dropping back to 6f after a 5f win on soft — watch whether the extra furlong on good ground blunts her finishing effort, as she needs the pace to collapse for her hold-up run to land.

Yellowstone Lake (W J Lee) returns after 45 days off and is a natural prominent type who cannot get that position here — if he settles well in midfield and travels powerfully in the first half of the race, that would be a significant positive sign for P Twomey's stable.

Likedbymike (Declan McDonogh) has raced exclusively over 5f in recent starts and steps up to 6f for the first time in this sequence — watch whether she is travelling within herself at halfway or being asked for effort early, which would indicate the trip is stretching her.

races.name: O'Neill & Co. Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for P J F Murphy whose recent form shows a string of mid-pack finishes at 8-10f on good ground; 34 days fresh is manageable, but sim-going record of 0 wins and 2 places from 15 comparable starts underscores limited upside in a race where closers need a strong pace.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Adam Grant picks up the ride on this hold-up type who carries a fade-in-finish flag; back in just seven days and has run exclusively at 8-18f on good ground, but the tendency to weaken late is a serious concern in a race likely to be run at a modest tempo.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's six-year-old hold-up type has three placed efforts at 8-9f on good ground in recent history and gets Jared Huggan's 7lb claim; the blinkers and tongue tie combination suggests the yard is trying to sharpen him up, and his 0W2P sim-going record gives him some each-way standing.

runners_data.name: Slaney Swagger
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with visor fitted who has placed at 8f on good ground three times; Aidan Melia has a 1/2 runner with this stable over 14 days, and the horse's 3rd on 13 days ago at 8f suggests he retains some form — but he needs the pace to stretch the race to use his stamina.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Ciaran Murphy returning seven days after latest start; best sim-going record is just 6/15 and she steps back from 10-16f which is a potential trip concern, making it hard to be enthusiastic even at a low weight of 136lbs.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner in this field, and with a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 her chance depends entirely on whether this pace map suits — it does, as she can control the race; last won over 8f on good ground 20 days ago and has the racing age and handler profile of a horse who can front-run competently at this level.

runners_data.name: Mehmar
runners_data.note: OR=52 hold-up type whose true style is hold-up, placed further forward on the map only because there are too many genuine closers to show at the rear; six days between runs is tight and all five recent efforts have been at shorter trips of 5-8f, making the mile a genuine stamina query.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Carries both a fade-in-finish warning and a redistribution note — the horse's natural home is at the rear of the field, not mid-division where the map places him; six consecutive non-winning efforts including several double-figure finishes on this going make it hard to identify a winning scenario.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose last five runs all ended in mid-to-rear finishes at 8-9f on good and standard ground; the fade-in-finish flag alongside his redistribution means the mile on a fair pace is not the recipe he needs to reverse those patterns.

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with Ruby Kinkaid's 7lb claim and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 — genuinely a rear-of-field type whose map position is a consequence of field crowding rather than natural racing style; best effort was a 2nd at Dundalk over 8f, and the switch to good turf from Dundalk standard needs treating with care.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: One of only three genuine prominent types in the race and a key tactical player for Patrick Foley; two placed efforts at 8f on standard and one win from 15 sim-going starts shows consistency in this position, and with OR=48 she is well-weighted to challenge Dinamine in the straight.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who is truly a rear-of-field runner, mapped to midfield only by redistribution; the form string of 00-008 and sim-going record of 0W0P from 7 comparable starts, combined with a fade warning, leaves very little to recommend her in this shape.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up performer whose most recent runs have all been at 6-7f — stepping up to a mile on good turf is a significant query, and the fade-in-finish tag plus redistribution means she is likely neither in her natural position nor ideally suited by this trip.

runners_data.name: Quarry Stone
runners_data.note: Adam Browne-Souza partners this hold-up type who has recorded a worst-of-recent-form 21st at 9f on good ground; the redistribution note confirms she cannot be expected to deliver a natural hold-up performance from mid-division, and the form is uniformly poor.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: 275 days off the track for Mrs Denise Foster is a stark fitness concern regardless of style; this hold-up type has historically run at 10-12f rather than a mile and is pushed to midfield only by field crowding — the lengthy absence makes her a significant risk on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Lorr's Girl
runners_data.note: Rodger Sweeney's hold-up mare has one win from 15 sim-going efforts and was last seen 42 days ago; genuinely runs from the rear and is only mapped to midfield because the field is stacked with closers — her trip form at 7-8f is consistent but the OR of 40 limits her ceiling.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Alan Casey's mount has run five times at 8-10f on good and soft, recording a best of 5th; this hold-up type's redistribution reflects field congestion at the rear rather than any tactical versatility, and the tongue tie and visor combination suggests the yard is searching for an answer.

runners_data.name: Mullacash Buzz
runners_data.note: One of only three genuine prominent types and therefore a critical race-shape player for Thomas Dowling; OR=40 is rock-bottom of the field but she has placed twice at 8f on good ground and has the tactical position to be involved from the front — the 20 days since last run is acceptable.

races.paceDynamic: Dinamine is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Famous Enough and Mullacash Buzz as the only other prominent types in a field of 18, faces no genuine pace duel — she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop through the mile on good turf at Naas. That comfortable lead is unlikely to be challenged hard enough to produce a truly punishing tempo, meaning the race will likely be run at an even clip that keeps the principals together into the straight rather than stringing the field out. The field's redistribution is significant: Mehmar, Lohengrin, Morning Approach, Akashaa, Peig Sayers, Pick A Window, Quarry Stone, Duchess Anne, Lorr's Girl and Master Garvey are all genuine hold-up horses pushed to midfield on the map because there are too many true closers to accommodate at the rear — several cannot get their natural position and that compresses the pack. This race shape — a lone leader, modest pace, well-bunched field — will most favour prominent horses and riders who can travel close to Dinamine and pounce in the straight, rather than late closers who depend on a truly strong gallop to reel in a leader that has never been pressured.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dinamine Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Dinamine gets to the front unchallenged and Famous Enough or Mullacash Buzz track her to challenge turning in on a fair gallop.
scenarios.body: Dinamine sets a comfortable pace that doesn't burn her out, leaving Famous Enough and Mullacash Buzz ideally positioned to strike when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs; with no pace pressure having softened the leader, the horse with the best tactical speed from close range wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dinamine Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that Dinamine's lead proves unassailable and hold-up horses lack the late burst to close.
scenarios.body: A crawling tempo turns this into a sprint from two furlongs out, where Dinamine's positional advantage becomes decisive and the field compresses too late to mount a meaningful challenge; prominent types who tracked throughout are the only realistic threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Gap Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively honest and hold-up horses find clear runs in the straight to run through the field.
scenarios.body: Despite most true hold-up runners being pushed wide on the map, a horse like Medieval Night or Slaney Swagger — naturally coming from behind — gets a clear run as the race quickens inside the final two furlongs; this scenario is discounted because several redistributed hold-up types are unlikely to be in their natural position to execute a true late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Famous Enough or Mullacash Buzz pressures Dinamine early, creating a falsely run race that collapses in the straight.
scenarios.body: An unexpected pace duel unsettles Dinamine and causes wholesale momentum loss turning for home, allowing a midfield horse stumbling onto an honest gallop to benefit; this outcome is the least likely given the clear absence of any aggressive pace challenger stepping forward.

watchPoints.text: Dinamine's early splits are crucial — if she gets to the front unchallenged in the first furlong at a crawling pace, she may never be headed and hold-up horses will have no tempo to exploit.

Famous Enough and Mullacash Buzz are the only horses likely to track Dinamine naturally; if either one makes a move on the leader turning in, it fundamentally alters the race shape and opens a window for closers.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Mehmar, Lohengrin, Morning Approach, Peig Sayers, Pick A Window among others — may cause significant crowding and traffic problems in mid-division on the turn, meaning clear runs cannot be assumed.

Medieval Night and Slaney Swagger are the hold-up types with the most meaningful placed form on comparable good-ground miles; watch whether they get a clean run in the straight as the field compresses if the pace is moderate.

Duchess Anne's 275-day layoff makes her a significant market mover to monitor — any meaningful support despite the absence would suggest stable confidence on reappearance and should prompt reassessment.

races.name: NFP Handicap

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Front-running handler whose recent form shows consistency in the places at 7f on good; Luke McAteer takes over and the trainer's cold 14-day strike rate (0/6) is a mild negative, but the uncontested lead in this field is a significant tactical asset that could offset modest form.

runners_data.name: Barbapapa
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's veteran (5/30 in 14 days) carries the tongue-tie and bounced badly last time at 7f on good (9th); a genuinely prominent-minded horse who will be squeezed out of his preferred early position by the traffic in front, making his task materially harder than his best form suggests.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft and placed over further, but his 10th last time at 7f on good is the relevant recent benchmark; Ronan Whelan inherits a horse who wants to race handy but will find that ground already occupied, and his 4-year-old profile at this trip on turf remains unproven at the top level of this race.

runners_data.name: Watch Tower
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's booking for a Gavin Lyons 3-year-old who has won over this exact course and distance on good ground (1/7f/GOO in hist) is the most compelling positional angle in the race; suited to track the leader naturally from a genuine prominent spot without redistribution pressure.

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up horse in the field — form figures of 804060 spell out a horse who is deeply out of form, and while his style theoretically suits a fast-run race, Nathan Crosse faces the task of motivating a seven-year-old who has finished in single figures five times running; tongue-and-pad headgear change noted.

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's handicapper has placed figures at 7f on both soft and good, but his last two runs produced 9ths and he hasn't won since an 8f success; a horse who wants to race prominently but will find himself shuffled back by the congested front rank, blunting his chance before the straight.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a Mrs Harrington 3-year-old who won over 6f and has placed twice on good ground; steps up to 7f for the second time and her form base at the shorter trip leaves the extra furlong a slight query, though her recent 3rd on good is a live staying-on profile if she settles in the compressed midfield.

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3-year-old won over this exact trip on good (1/7f/GOO) most recently and Ben Coen's experience is a clear plus; a natural front-to-midfield horse who will face the same overcrowding as the other redistributed types — getting back into his preferred groove from a compromised position will determine whether his recent winning form translates here.

races.paceDynamic: Little Empire is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, shapes to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Naas's flat 7f on good ground. Watch Tower is the only genuine prominent type alongside Little Empire who can realistically secure an early position without fighting for it, giving the front rank a settled, uncrowded look. The displaced prominent horses — Barbapapa, Spodo Komodo, Eddie G, and Contrary To Law — are all natural front-to-midfield types who will struggle to get their preferred ground and will race closer than their mapped positions suggest, compressing the midfield and creating a bunched chasing pack rather than a clean pace hierarchy. This field holds more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate, and Little Empire plus Watch Tower are most likely to actually secure the front positions; the redistribution of Barbapapa, Spodo Komodo, Eddie G, and Contrary To Law into an uncomfortable midfield cluster leaves this race firmly in the hands of the horses capable of travelling efficiently behind an uncontested, honest gallop — a tactical verdict that rewards prominent trackers and mid-division horses with a clean run, rather than genuine hold-up finishers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Little Empire sets an uncontested, honest pace and Watch Tower tracks without pressure, the pair dictate tempo and kick into clear air.
scenarios.body: Little Empire controls fractions without burning fuel, and Watch Tower's course-winning form over 7f on good ground puts him in the prime stalking spot to collar or match the leader late; a genuine lead scenario at a sane tempo is hardest to peg back when the midfield is congested and hold-up horses have nowhere to accelerate from.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Collapse, Finisher Arrives
scenarios.trigger: If the true prominent types (Barbapapa, Spodo Komodo, Contrary To Law) push forward from their uncomfortable positions and inject pace, the early fractions quicken and the front end exhausts.
scenarios.body: A faster-run race stretches the field and opens a gap for a horse able to come with one sustained run from off the pace; Contrary To Law's recent 7f win on good at this sort of trip and Blues Emperor, while in poor current form, carry the profile for this shape — though Blues Emperor's weak recent runs make this a slim hope.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Compression, Lucky Run Through
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched midfield of redistributed prominent types blocks passages in the straight, a horse who finds a clear rail or gap delivers the decisive run.
scenarios.body: With five naturally prominent horses compressed into a tight chasing group, the horse who gets a clean outside or inner run through in the final 2f benefits disproportionately; Thenandnow's compact action and recent 3rd on good ground over further than she's run today, combined with Shane Foley's positional awareness, makes her the most likely beneficiary of a fortunate gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Blues Emperor, the only true hold-up runner, gets a clear passage from off the back, he arrives late to mop up weakening rivals.
scenarios.body: Blues Emperor is the sole genuine H-style runner in the field and the only horse whose profile truly suits a fast-run, strongly-paced 7f — but his recent form figures of 8-0-4-0-6 are deeply discouraging and make this outcome reliant on a significant form reversal.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tower (Colin Keane) has winning course-and-distance form on good ground and is the only genuine prominent type who can slot in behind Little Empire without a fight — track his early positioning closely as he is the pivot horse for the dominant scenario.

Barbapapa, Spodo Komodo, Eddie G, and Contrary To Law are all natural front-runners who cannot all get to the positions they want — watch for crowding and bumping in the first furlong as they sort out the order, which could unsettle any of them before the race has properly begun.

Little Empire's trainer Anthony McCann has returned 0 from 6 over the last 14 days — if the horse is slightly below his best, the uncontested lead that underpins the dominant scenario evaporates and the race shape opens up considerably.

Contrary To Law (Ben Coen) arrives on the back of a 7f good-ground win and is the most dangerous of the redistributed horses if he manages to get closer to his natural prominent position than the map suggests — monitor his draw and early stride.

Blues Emperor is fitted with tongue-tie and pad headgear as the sole genuine hold-up runner; in a race where the pace is likely to be controlled rather than strong, his style is at its weakest — only relevant if the compressed prominent pack creates an unexpectedly fast early tempo.

races.name: Naas Racecourse Race

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Solid 7f Good-ground form with two wins and multiple placings at this trip and going combination, and trainer Sheila Lavery is without a winner in her last 14-day window (0/3); a natural prominent type, the horse ends up mapped to midfield in this shape purely because Suzie Songs and Phenomenal Filly are better placed to secure the forward positions in a four-runner field, so Fort Vega may find itself racing slightly off its preferred rhythm.|

runners_data.name: Dark Willow
runners_data.note: 245 days off the track is a serious red flag, compounded by a form string of 80408- that shows consistent fading in the finish — the warning tag is well earned; a hold-up style that is the lone closer in this field, but her chance of making up meaningful ground on a sustainable pace over 7f Good looks very slim without any recent fitness evidence.|

runners_data.name: Phenomenal Filly
runners_data.note: P Twomey's yard is in good form (2/9 over 14 days) and W J Lee rides, with a cracking placed effort at 2/7f on Good just 13 days ago keeping her very fresh in the market; she wears headgear (hood) and has winning form over this exact trip and going, making her the most natural challenger to Suzie Songs if the pace is honest enough to suit a close-travelling prominent type.|

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace setter for G M Lyons, who is firing on all cylinders with six winners from 25 runners over 14 days, and Colin Keane is the standout jockey booking in this field; two wins from six starts on Good ground and a form figure of 1 at 6f suggests she has the raw ability to dictate and hold, though the [STYLE_FIT] tag notes she is also somewhat racing out of the expected mapped role, meaning if something goes wrong tactically her chance is not nailed-on.|

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the confirmed front runner in this small four-runner field and, with only three rivals to contend with, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 7f trip on Good ground at Naas. Fort Vega and Phenomenal Filly are both natural prominent types who will press forward behind her, creating a race run at honest but not brutal fractions — enough to test stamina without burning off the pace setters. Dark Willow is the lone hold-up type but carries a serious form concern with repeated fading patterns, making her tactical role largely irrelevant to the outcome. This race shape — a controlled front-runner allowed to roll along without genuine pace pressure — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than those who must close from off the pace. The field holds more prominent types than the positions allow: Fort Vega, a genuine prominent racer, has been redistributed to midfield in the shape map because Suzie Songs and Phenomenal Filly are more likely to secure the forward berths in this small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Suzie Songs Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs gets her favoured prominent lead role unchallenged and dictates a measured pace, she dictates fractions from the outset and simply outstays the small field into the straight. A horse allowed to bowl along on Good ground over a trip she has won at before, with Colin Keane in the saddle for an in-form yard, is very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Duel, Late Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Phenomenal Filly hustles up to pressurise Suzie Songs from the off, raising the tempo and turning it into a proper contest. Both prominent types empty close home, allowing the horse who travels most smoothly off the pace to pick them off — Phenomenal Filly's stronger recent form and Good-ground record at this trip makes her the likeliest beneficiary if Suzie Songs is emptied.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fort Vega Threads Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fort Vega is allowed to creep into the race from off the pace and the leaders tie each other up enough to open a gap. Fort Vega has form figures of 2-1 at 7f on Good ground and Rory Cleary is capable of a patient ride, but the horse's natural style is prominent so it is racing partially out of role here, tempering confidence in this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely extreme and the leaders come back to the field, giving Dark Willow or a fading front runner a chance. Dark Willow's record — repeated finishes of 8th, 14th and 12th — and 245 days off the track make this scenario extremely unlikely to materialise in her favour.

watchPoints.text: Phenomenal Filly's jockey W J Lee may press Suzie Songs harder than expected from the off — if she sends her mount to the lead or sits a half-length off throughout, watch for the fractions to quicken markedly mid-race.

Fort Vega's redistribution to midfield means Rory Cleary will need to make a conscious choice about whether to fight for position or accept a hold-up role — an uncharacteristic tardy start or crowding at the break could compromise Fort Vega's race entirely.

Dark Willow's 245-day absence and repeated fading pattern mean she should be monitored for early signs of fatigue or reluctance; if she drops away quickly after 3f it confirms she needed the run and affects how much ground she gives away to the front two.

With only four runners, the pace dynamic is entirely dependent on whether Suzie Songs is allowed a free rein — watch the first two furlongs to see if Phenomenal Filly challenges for the lead or settles in behind, as that one decision shapes the entire race outcome.
